title: The Small Shop on Wheels
title_ja: 車輪のついた小さな店
fact_notes: 登場人物・出来事は架空の教材例。実在の調査結果ではない。リンクは制作台帳であり実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A fruit seller named Omar wanted to reach people living outside town.
sentences.ja: オマルという果物屋は町の外に住む人にも商品を届けたかった。

sentences.en: He could not afford to rent a second shop.
sentences.ja: 二つ目の店舗を借りる余裕がなかった。

sentences.en: Instead, he considered selling fruit from a small vehicle.
sentences.ja: 代わりに小さな車から果物を販売することを考えた。

sentences.en: His sister offered to help him plan a weekly route.
sentences.ja: 姉妹が毎週の巡回経路を考えるのを手伝うと申し出た。

sentences.en: At first, Omar selected villages by looking at a map.
sentences.ja: 最初オマルは地図を見て村を選んだ。

sentences.en: He chose the places that were farthest from his shop.
sentences.ja: 自分の店から最も離れた場所を選んだ。

sentences.en: However, his sister suggested speaking with local residents before deciding.
sentences.ja: しかし姉妹は決める前に地元住民と話すことを提案した。

sentences.en: Some villages already had enough places to buy fresh fruit.
sentences.ja: 新鮮な果物を買える店が十分にある村もあった。

sentences.en: They discovered that a nearby village had recently lost its only food shop.
sentences.ja: 近くの村が最近唯一の食料品店を失ったと分かった。

sentences.en: Several residents asked whether Omar could visit on Tuesday afternoons.
sentences.ja: 数人の住民は火曜の午後に来られるか尋ねた。

sentences.en: They also explained which products they would probably purchase.
sentences.ja: どの品を買いそうかも説明した。

sentences.en: Omar adjusted his route and prepared smaller amounts of each fruit.
sentences.ja: オマルは経路を調整し、果物を少量ずつ用意した。

sentences.en: After a month, he examined his records of sales and travel expenses.
sentences.ja: 1か月後、売上と移動費の記録を調べた。

sentences.en: The village visits earned less money than his busiest market days.
sentences.ja: 村への訪問の売上は最も忙しい市場の日より少なかった。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the new route was affordable and regular customers returned each week.
sentences.ja: それでも新しい経路は費用を賄え、常連客は毎週戻ってきた。

sentences.en: He decided to continue visiting the village while monitoring his costs.
sentences.ja: 費用を確認しながら村への訪問を続けることにした。

sentences.en: Omar did not simply look for the largest possible market.
sentences.ja: オマルは単に最大の市場を探したわけではなかった。

sentences.en: He looked for a place where his service would meet a real need.
sentences.ja: 自分のサービスが実際の必要性を満たす場所を探した。

sentences.en: His experience showed him the value of listening before investing money.
sentences.ja: 経験からお金を投資する前に話を聞く価値を学んだ。

sentences.en: For his business, a useful route was more important than a long one.
sentences.ja: 彼の事業では長い経路より役立つ経路の方が重要だった。

vocabulary.definition: a machine used to carry people or goods
a way taken from one place to another
people who live in a place
with a good chance of happening
received money for work or sales
not costing more than one can pay
using money in hope of a future benefit

questions.prompt: Why did Omar continue the route?
options: It earned more than every market day.
The village forced him to visit.
The costs were manageable and customers returned.
questions.explanation_ja: 費用を賄え常連客もいた。

options: The most distant market is always the best.

A business should never change its plans.
